rows.speaker: قائل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes al-ʿaṣr as time or the age (al-dahr).
rows.anchor: الأول : أنه الدهر ، واحتج هذا القائل بوجوه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet swore by time and recited “by time and its vicissitudes”; al-Rāzī rejects that as Qurʾānic recitation because it would invalidate prayer, treating it as exegesis.
rows.anchor: ما روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أقسم بالدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Time contains astonishing opposites, and its divisions and changing states make it impossible for reason straightforwardly to judge it either nonexistent or existent.
rows.anchor: أن الدهر مشتمل على الأعاجيب لأنه يحصل فيه السراء والضراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thousand wasted years can be redeemed by repentance in life’s final moment, making that moment more valuable than the preceding lifespan.
rows.anchor: فلو ضيعت ألف سنة ، ثم تبث في اللمحة الأخيرة من العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because time is a fundamental blessing, the oath warns that night and day are opportunities people waste, as stated in 25:62.
rows.anchor: فكأن الدهر والزمان من جملة أصول النعم ، فلذلك أقسم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾān 6:12–13 pairs the ownership of places with what inhabits night and day; time is nobler than place, so the oath is by the nobler half of God’s dominion.
rows.anchor: وقد بينا هناك أن الزمان أعلم وأشرف من المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People blame time’s vicissitudes for their losses, but the oath shows time itself is a blessing without fault; the defective loser is the human being.
rows.anchor: فكأنه تعالى أقسم على أن الدهر والعصر نعمة حاصلة لا عيب فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As time passes, a person’s lifespan shrinks; without compensating gain, that loss explains the next verse’s judgment that humanity is in loss.
rows.anchor: ذكر العصر الذي بمضيه ينتقص عمرك ، فإذا لم يكن في مقابلته كسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s paradox is that people rejoice in passing days although each day cuts into their remaining lifespan; the cited poem expresses this.
rows.anchor: إنا لنفرح بالأيام نقطعها *** وكل يوم مضى نقص من الأجل

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim interprets al-ʿaṣr as one of the day’s two ends, the late afternoon.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني ) : وهو قول أبي مسلم : المراد بالعصر أحد طرفي النهار

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Like dawn, evening displays divine power: dawn resembles resurrection, while evening resembles the world’s ruin in death; these are witnesses against the heedless person who fails to judge.
rows.anchor: أقسم تعالى بالعصر كما أقسم بالضحى لما فيهما جميعا من دلائل القدرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan compares afternoon to markets nearing closure: one who has not earned before going home faces dependents’ claims; likewise the world nears judgment while people remain unprepared and liable to answer for blessings and wrongs.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن رحمه الله : إنما أقسم بهذا الوقت تنبيها على أن الأسواق قد دنا وقت انقطاعها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says one who swears falsely after the afternoon prayer will not be addressed or regarded by God on Judgment Day; al-Rāzī cites it as evidence that this time is honored.
rows.anchor: من حلف بعد العصر كاذبا لا يكلمه الله ولا ينظر إليه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿaṣr warns the loser while some daylight remains, urging repentance and recovery; in contrast, the morning oath concerns the successful and movement toward arrival.
rows.anchor: فكما أقسم في حق الرابح بالضحى فكذا أقسم في حق الخاسر بالعصر

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: An unnamed early Muslim said an ice seller taught him the sūra’s meaning by crying that his capital was melting: passing time consumes life without earnings and leaves one in loss.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض السلف : تعلمت معنى السورة من بائع الثلج كان يصيح

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil interprets al-ʿaṣr as the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: القول الثالث : وهو قول مقاتل : أراد صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One argument for the afternoon prayer interpretation is its identification with the “middle prayer” in 2:238, reportedly specified as afternoon prayer in Ḥafṣa’s codex.
rows.anchor: أقسم بصلاة العصر لفضلها بدليل قوله : { والصلاة الوسطى } صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second scriptural argument identifies the prayer mentioned in 5:106 as the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل في قوله : { تحبسونهما من بعد الصلاة فيقسمان بالله } إنها صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet likened missing the afternoon prayer to losing one’s family and property; this is cited to establish its merit.
rows.anchor: من فاتته صلاة العصر فكأنما وتر أهله وماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Performing the afternoon prayer is especially difficult because people are occupied with trade and livelihood late in the day.
rows.anchor: أن التكليف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجاراتهم ومكاسبهم آخر النهار

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A reported woman’s confession recounts adultery, killing her child in a vinegar jar, and selling the vinegar; the Prophet assigns punishments and rebukes her for having left the afternoon prayer, underscoring its gravity.
rows.anchor: أما الزنا فعليك الرجم ، أما قتل الولد فجزاؤه جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afternoon prayer closes the day’s acts of worship like repentance closes one’s deeds; because endings matter, it merits special emphasis, and performing it properly turns loss into profit, as the exception says.
rows.anchor: أن صلاة العصر بها يحصل ختم طاعات النهار ، فهي كالتوبة بها يختم الأعمال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet listed among three people whom God will neither regard, address, nor purify a man who falsely swears after the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة لا ينظر الله إليهم يوم القيامة ولا يكلمهم ولا يزكيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although prayer is a human act, God may swear by it because it is a noble institution He commanded, rather than because it is the worshippers’ act.
rows.anchor: أنه ليس قسما من حيث إنها فعلنا ، بل من حيث إنها أمر شريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation takes al-ʿaṣr as the era of the Prophet and his community, based on a report comparing the wages of earlier religious communities and Muslims.
rows.anchor: القول الرابع : أنه قسم بزمان الرسول عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s parable says Jews worked from dawn to noon for one qīrāṭ, Christians from noon to afternoon for one, and his community from afternoon to sunset for two; God calls the greater wage His bounty.
rows.anchor: من يعمل من الفجر إلى الظهر بقيراط ، فعملت اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s era, place, and lifespan are respectively sworn by in 103:1, 90:2, and 15:72; as his setting is honored, so is he, and the oath rebukes those who rejected his invitation.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قال : وعصرك وبلدك وعمرك ، وذلك كله كالظرف له

rows.speaker: من قال : العمل غير داخل في مسمى الإيمان
rows.claim: Those who exclude deeds from the definition of faith argue that conjunction of faith and righteous deeds would otherwise be redundant; unlike emphatic mention of a class’s noblest member, righteous works are not faith’s noblest subtype.
rows.anchor: احتج من قال : العمل غير داخل في مسمى الإيمان ، بأن الله تعالى عطف عمل الصالحات

rows.speaker: من قال : العمل غير داخل في مسمى الإيمان
rows.claim: They distinguish this verse from cases that single out a particularly honored member after a general category, such as 33:7 and 2:98.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { وإذا أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح }

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥalīmī accepts repetition here: although faith does not include righteous deeds, the latter include faith and the following mutual exhortation, making the earlier wording dispensable.
rows.anchor: قال الحليمي : هذا التكرير واقع لا محالة ، لأن الإيمان وإن لم يشتمل

rows.speaker: الأولون
rows.claim: The first group replies that repetition for emphasis is possible, but its being possible does not erase the presumption against repetition, which supports their argument.
rows.anchor: إنا لا نمنع ورود التكرير لأجل التأكيد ، لكن الأصل عدمه

rows.speaker: القاطعون بوعيد الفساق
rows.claim: Those who insist the threat against grave sinners is fulfilled argue that only people possessing both faith and righteous deeds escape loss; whoever lacks either faces loss in this world and the next, so the saved are few and fear should be intense.
rows.anchor: احتج القاطعون بوعيد الفساق بهذه الآية ، قالوا : الآية دلت على أن الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception consoles believers for lost life and youth: their deeds have brought them something better than those years.
rows.anchor: أنه تسلية للمؤمن من فوت عمره وشبابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever draws a person to obey God is righteousness; whatever distracts from God toward something else is corruption.
rows.anchor: أن كل ما دعاك إلى طاعة الله فهو الصلاح

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer from calling deeds righteous that their goodness lies in benefits inherent in them, not merely in a divine command.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : تسمية الأعمال بالصالحات تنبيه على أن وجه حسنها

rows.speaker: الأشعرية
rows.claim: The Ashʿarites answer that God calls the deeds righteous without specifying whether their goodness comes from inherent benefits or from command.
rows.anchor: وأجابت الأشعرية بأن الله تعالى وصفها بكونها صالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names the cause of profit but not its outcome, and the outcome of loss but not its cause: loss can arise through sinful action or omitted obedience, whereas profit requires action.
rows.anchor: إن الخسر كما يحصل بالفعل ، وهو الإقدام على المعصية يحصل بالترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the text leaves loss vague but spells out profit, a presentation fitting divine generosity.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى في جانب الخسر أبهم ولم يفصل ، وفي جانب الربح فصل وبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because believers love obedience, they do not restrict themselves to personal good works; they urge others to follow the same way and become causes of others’ obedience.
rows.anchor: لا يقتصرون على ما يخصهم بل يوصون غيرهم بمثل طريقتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty to guide one’s household parallels 66:6; exhortation to truth encompasses the whole religion in knowledge and practice.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه قال تعالى : { يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exhortation to patience includes making oneself endure the difficulty of duties and avoid prohibitions, since doing disliked things and restraining desired things are both hard.
rows.anchor: والتواصي بالصبر يدخل فيه حمل النفس على مشقة التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salvation requires all four qualities; alongside personal faith and good works, people owe others calling to religion, sincere counsel, enjoining right, forbidding wrong, and wishing for them what they wish for themselves.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك على أن النجاة معلقة بمجموع هذه الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repetition of mutual exhortation assigns one clause to calling people to God and persistence in truth, and the other to enjoining right and forbidding wrong.
rows.anchor: ثم كرر التواصي ليضمن الأول الدعاء إلى الله ، والثاني الثبات عليه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar prayed that God show mercy to whoever points out his faults.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر : رحم الله من أهدى إلي عيوبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth is burdensome and accompanied by trials, which is why it is paired with mutual exhortation.
rows.anchor: دلت الآية على أن الحق ثقيل ، وأن المحن تلازمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense form tawāṣaw praises what they did and signals their desire to persist in it in the future.
rows.anchor: إنما قال : { وتواصوا } ولم يقل : ويتواصون

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr recited bi-l-ṣabr with a slight, incomplete quality on the bāʾ; Abū ʿAlī says this fits a pause, and only rarely a connected reading treated like pause.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو : { بالصبر } بشم الباء شيئا من الحرف ، لا يشبع

rows.speaker: سلام بن المنذر
rows.claim: Salām ibn al-Mundhir is reported to read wa-l-ʿaṣr with kasra on ṣād; al-Rāzī explains it as a pause caused by breath or another impediment, not connected speech treated as a pause.
rows.anchor: ما يروى عن سلام بن المنذر أنه قرأ ، والعصر بكسر الصاد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read arayta with the hamza omitted. Al-Zajjāj disfavours it because Arabs do not say rīt for raʾayt, though an initial interrogative can ease hamza deletion; the cited verse witnesses the form.
rows.anchor: قرأ بعضهم { أريت } بحذف الهمزة ، قال الزجاج : وهذا ليس بالاختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetic line “ṣāḥ hal rayta” is cited as evidence for the expression’s usage.
rows.anchor: صاح هل ريت أو سمعت براع *** رد في الضرع ما قرى في العلاب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read araytaka with an added second-person marker, like the wording in 17:62.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ( أرأيتك ) بزيادة حرف الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arayta asks whether one has recognized who denies recompense; if not, the following verse identifies him as the person who pushes the orphan.
rows.anchor: معناه هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء من هو ، فإن لم تعرفه : ( فهو الذي يدع اليتيم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although phrased as a question, arayta intensifies astonishment, like asking what someone did and why he exposed himself to it.
rows.anchor: هذا اللفظ وإن كان في صورة الاستفهام ، لكن الغرض بمثله المبالغة في التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the address as directed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنه خطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes it an address to every rational person: after clear proofs, how could someone risk everlasting punishment without purpose or trade the enduring great for fleeting worldly gain?
rows.anchor: وقيل : بل خطاب لكل عاقل أي أرأيت يا عاقل هذا الذي يكذب بالدين

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the verse was revealed about Abū Sufyān, who slaughtered two camels weekly and struck an orphan with his stick when the child asked for meat.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن جريج : نزلت في أبي سفيان كان ينحر جزورين في كل أسبوع

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says it was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī, whose traits joined denial of Judgment Day with vile conduct.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي ، وكان من صفته الجمع

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra as the person about whom the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī transmits that it concerned Abū Jahl, guardian of a naked orphan who asked for his own money and was pushed away; Quraysh mockingly sent him to seek Muhammad’s intercession, and Abū Jahl gave the money only because he feared the Prophet’s spears.
rows.anchor: وحكى الماوردي أنها نزلت في أبي جهل ، وروي أنه كان وصيا ليتيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about a hypocrite combining miserliness and ostentation.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في منافق جمع بين البخل والمراءاة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators understand al-dīn here as reckoning and recompense; al-Rāzī favors this because someone denying Islam might still do good if convinced of resurrection, whereas unrestrained vice indicates denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أكثر المفسرين . أن المراد أرأيت الذي يكذب بالحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers “reckoning and recompense”: denial of resurrection explains persistent wrongdoing better than denial of Islam alone.
rows.anchor: وحمله على هذا الوجه أولى لأن من ينكر الإسلام قد يأتي بالأفعال الحميدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes al-dīn as religion and Islam, including denial of God, prophethood, resurrection, or any law; unqualified “religion” in Islamic and Qurʾānic usage means Islam, while other religions require qualification.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد من يكذب بنفس الدين والإسلام إما لأنه كان منكرا للصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation says false doctrines are not truly religion, since religion means submission to God, while such doctrines submit to appetite or conjecture.
rows.anchor: هذه المقالات الباطلة ليست بدين ، لأن الدين هو الخضوع لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A general reading applies to anyone who denies the Resurrection: without hope of reward or fear of punishment, people would pursue desires and leave prohibitions unchecked, making denial of the afterlife a root of unbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: أن إقدام الإنسان على الطاعات وإحجامه عن المحظورات إنما يكون للرغبة في الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orphan-pushing is the first of two traits identifying the denier of religion, and it is an outward action.
rows.anchor: ذكر في تعريف من يكذب الدين وصفين ( أحدهما ) : من باب الأفعال وهو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition from mistreating orphans and withholding food to prayer contrasts dealings with creatures against service to the Creator: prayer without humility is an even clearer sign of hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: لأن الإيذاء والمنع من النفع معاملة مع المخلوق ، أما الصلاة فإنها خدمة للخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of orphan abuse and failure to urge feeding prompts the question whether prayer prevents wrongdoing; the answer is that ostentation and heedlessness make such prayer itself corrupt.
rows.anchor: أليس إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ؟ فقال له : الصلاة كيف تنهاه عن هذا الفعل المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglect of compassion toward God’s creatures and neglect of reverence toward God complete the person’s misery, hence the warning.
rows.anchor: تقصير فيما يرجع إلى الشفقة على خلق الله ، وسهوه في الصلاة تقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl is used for a grave crime, as in warnings in 83:1, 2:79, and 104:1.
rows.anchor: إن هذا اللفظ إنما يستعمل عند الجريمة الشديدة كقوله : { ويل للمطففين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says each person in Hell laments according to his crime—status-seeking, tribal zeal, or prayer—so one should say on hearing the verse, “Woe to me if God does not forgive me.”
rows.anchor: ويروى أن كل أحد ينوح في النار بحسب جريمته ، فقائل يقول : ويلي من حب الشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened traits are heedlessness about prayer, ostentation, and withholding small assistance; all are sins, but do not ordinarily make someone a hypocrite, prompting exegetes to explain the severe threat.
rows.anchor: الآية دالة على حصول التهديد العظيم بفعل ثلاثة أمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relied-upon answer restricts the warning to hypocrites who perform these acts; it implies disbelievers incur extra punishment for forbidden acts and neglected duties, supporting al-Shāfiʿī’s view that they are addressed by the branches of religious law.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { فويل للمصلين } أي فويل للمصلين من المنافقين الذين يأتون بهذه الأفعال

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports Ibn ʿAbbās’s distinction: “in their prayer” could threaten believers, but “about their prayer” describes those who forget prayer and are empty of it.
rows.anchor: ما رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس أنه لو قال الله : في صلاتهم ساهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī calls that explanation weak: treating heedlessness about prayer as abandoning it conflicts with their being called worshippers, and abandonment alone is neither hypocrisy nor unbelief.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف لأن السهو عن الصلاة لا يجوز أن يكون مفسرا بترك الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible reply says they are misleaders outwardly but have forgotten prayer inwardly, like the hypocrites described in 4:142 as lazy, ostentatious, and remembering God only a little.
rows.anchor: كما قال : { وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reply distinguishes a hypocrite who forgets God throughout prayer from a believer who may become heedless in only some parts; this makes heedlessness in prayer a believer’s lapse and heedlessness about prayer a disbeliever’s trait.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن السهو في الصلاة من أفعال المؤمن والسهو عن الصلاة من أفعال الكافر

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص ومسروق والحسن ومقاتل
rows.claim: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Masrūq, al-Ḥasan, and Muqātil say the heedless are those who fail to observe prayer times and conditions and do not care whether they pray.
rows.anchor: وهو قول سعد بن أبي وقاص ومسروق والحسن ومقاتل

rows.speaker: كثير من العلماء
rows.claim: Many scholars hold that the Prophet never lapsed in prayer; rather, God allowed him to perform the act of a forgetful person so that he could demonstrate the law, since practical demonstration is stronger.
rows.anchor: فقال كثير من العلماء : إنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ما سها ، لكن الله تعالى أذن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s and Companions’ prayer lapses are repaired either by prostration of forgetfulness or by sunnah and voluntary prayers.
rows.anchor: سهو الرسول والصحابة وذلك منجبر تارة بسجود السهو وتارة بالسنن والنوافل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second kind is inattentiveness during prayer, including failure to keep religious knowledge and intentions present.
rows.anchor: ما يكون في الصلاة من الغفلة وعدم استحضار المعارف والنيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third kind is leaving prayer without making it up and taking it outside its time; the hypocrite’s performative prayer is worse than simply abandoning prayer because it mocks religion.
rows.anchor: الترك لا إلى قضاء والإخراج عن الوقت ، ومن ذلك صلاة المنافق وهي شر من ترك الصلاة
